title: THE GIANT MOVED FIRST.
paragraphs: THE GIANT MOVED FIRST.

Steel clanked.
Dust rose.
Forty days of intimidation walking down that valley.
Goliath stepped forward again—towering, armored, roaring like a war drum.
“Send me a man!”
But no one moved.

Not the soldiers.
Not the commanders.
Not even the king.
Fear had frozen an entire army.
Then a shepherd boy arrived with bread and cheese.

David was not supposed to be there.
He wasn’t a soldier.
He had no armor.
No sword.

Just a sling.
Five stones.
And a heart that burned with holy anger.
When he heard the giant mocking the living God, something in him snapped awake.
“Who is this uncircumcised Philistine,” David said, “that he should defy the armies of the living God?” (1 Samuel 17:26)
Here’s the moment most people miss.
When the giant started walking forward…
David didn’t retreat.
Scripture says:
“David ran quickly toward the battle line to meet him.” (1 Samuel 17:48)

Not slowly.
Not cautiously.
Ran.
Toward the giant.
Because David understood something the army forgot:
The battle wasn’t David vs. Goliath.
It was Goliath vs. the Lord.

One stone flew.
One giant fell.
And the ground shook with the sound of God defending His name.
Listen carefully, my friend.
Your giant may look like:

• addiction that keeps whispering your name
• shame from a past you cannot erase
• a marriage hanging by a thread
• fear that has paralyzed your faith
But giants fall when faith runs forward.
And the greatest giant humanity ever faced was sin itself.

We could not defeat it.
We stood helpless in the valley.
Then another Son of David stepped forward.
Jesus Christ ran toward the ultimate battlefield—the cross.

Sin mocked.
Death roared.
Hell celebrated.
But on the third day…
the Giant fell.
Through His death and resurrection, Jesus crushed the enemy we could never defeat.
That means the giants in your life do not get the final word.
Grace does.
Hope does.
Christ does.
So today, lift your head.
The God who stood with David still fights for His people.
And the valley you fear may become the place where God shows His power.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
